source.stem:
Multiple choice questions.

System of equations

$$
\left\{ \begin{array}{l} 3 x + 4 y = 5, \\ - 7 x + 9 y = - \frac {5}{2} \end{array} \right.
$$

The solution is ( ).

(A) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 2,\\ y = -0.25 \end{array} \right.$

(B) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -5.5,\\ y = 4 \end{array} \right.$

(C) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 1,\\ y = 0.5 \end{array} \right.$

(D) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -1,\\ y = -0.5 \end{array} \right.$

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: Thread-gap is the label that belongs on this item, so 'Predict whether a thread-gap pattern reaches every peg from the' is answered as thread-gap rather than number of pegs.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: Every-peg traversal is what produces co-primality of peg count and thread-gap, so the usual direction of this relation is run backwards — on the item about Predict whether a thread-gap pattern reaches every peg.

mx.name: mechanism_conflation
mx.teacher_note: number of pegs is settled by running 'Decide whether two numbers are co-prime or a safe pair by checking': Two numbers are co-prime when they have no common factor other than 1; a treasure pair is — on the item about Predict whether a thread-gap pattern reaches every peg.

intelligence.enrichment: In cyclic thread art, tying to every fixed gap reaches every peg when the number of pegs and the thread-gap are co-prime; if they share a common factor greater than 1, the thread repeats a smaller cycle and misses some pegs.
